entities.name: Azzo VII d'Este
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Azzo VII d'Este, known as "Novello," was a pivotal Italian nobleman and military commander who served as Marquis of Este and, crucially, as the first undisputed *signore* (lord) of Ferrara from 1240 until his death in 1264. His reign marked a definitive turning point in the political landscape of Emilia-Romagna, solidifying the Este family's dynastic control over Ferrara and establishing a formidable Guelph stronghold amidst the turbulent Guelph-Ghibelline conflicts of the 13th century. He was a leading figure in the Lombard League, instrumental in resisting the imperial ambitions of Frederick II and challenging the expansionist Ghibelline power of Ezzelino III da Romano.

Azzo VII's ascendancy to power in Ferrara was a hard-won victory, achieved after years of struggle against imperial forces and local Ghibelline factions. Following the expulsion of Salinguerra II Torelli in 1240, Azzo, supported by Pope Gregory IX and the Venetian Republic, established the Este family's hereditary lordship, ending the city's communal independence. He then dedicated his military prowess to the Guelph cause, leading campaigns against Frederick II's forces and, most notably, serving as Captain-General of the Guelph League against the tyrannical Ezzelino III da Romano, whose brutal rule terrorized much of Veneto and eastern Lombardy. Azzo's forces played a significant role in the decisive siege of Padua in 1256 and the subsequent defeat and death of Ezzelino at the Battle of Cassano in 1259, an event that profoundly reshaped the political map of Northern Italy.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Azzo VII d'Este was a critical figure in establishing one of Italy's most enduring *signorie*, the Este lordship of Ferrara, which lasted for over three centuries. His military leadership against Ezzelino III da Romano also significantly impacted the regional balance of power in 13th-century Northern Italy.
